request.spec: Show on each period the count of claims belonging to it (VOID and DELETED claims left out).
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
Show on each period the count of claims belonging to it (VOID and DELETED claims left out).

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
Each period row now shows how many claims belong to it, with void and deleted claims left out. All 4 tests in the spec pass when run with `bin/e2e`.

A claim belongs to a period when its due-by date falls inside the period's days. That's the same rule the claim row already uses for its period column. It is not the claim's own date. That's why, in the test, the claim dated 2026-03-15 is counted in P1 (03-01 to 03-10), not P2. Drafts, claims in review, and open, pending and settled claims all count.

The change is only in the front end; I didn't touch the server or the stored data.
- **`people-list.ts`:** a new `periodClaimCounts` counts each period's claims from the claims already loaded on the screen. Period due-totals are worked out the same way. In as-of view it works from the claims as they stood that day.
- **`period-form.ts`:** the periods table has a new "Claims" column showing the count, marked `period-claims-count`.

Nothing new is written to the audit file, and the test doesn't expect anything.
